The intraocular pressure measured by Goldmann tonometer was 15 mm Hg in both eyes.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Giant Cell Tumor (GCT) of the right inferior rectus muscle
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old man presented with a 3-year history of vertical diplopia and selective visual acuity loss on upward gaze (hand motion/10 cm) despite normal forward gaze vision (20/20). Physical examination revealed right eye proptosis (3 mm on Hertel exophthalmometry), upward globe displacement, and compromised supraduction and infraduction of the right eye. Orbital CT imaging demonstrated enlargement of the right inferior rectus muscle infiltrated by a muscle-density tumor measuring 11 × 17 × 7 mm³ that displaced the globe upward. Surgical biopsy and histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of giant cell tumor, characterized by an encapsulated lesion with large nested or cord-like cells with small nuclei and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. Immunohistochemistry showed strong expression of CD68, S100, and vimentin, weak Ki67 positivity, and negative cytokeratin staining. The tumor was surgically excised via a transconjunctival approach along the inferior rectus muscle. Intraoperatively, the tumor was completely separated from muscle tissue due to its pseudoencapsular nature. Gross pathology revealed a firm, fibrotic, nodule-like, pale-colored mass. Immediate post-operative assessment showed no significant improvement in globe mobility, with longer-term follow-up recommended.
